business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Shipbuilding of Deep-Sea Dry Cargo and Container Vessels

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: Independent State of Samoa (Malo Sa'oloto Tuto'atasi o Samoa)
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa - Offshore International Companies Regime (Registrar of International Companies, MCIL)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common law heritage with statutory offshore company regime; customary law overlay for non-commercial matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: WTO Membership (Samoa acceded 10 May 2012) - MFN trade framework applicable to PRC commercial relations
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus; in force 13 December 2020)
Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Independent State of Samoa on Economic and Technical Cooperation (successive protocols since 1996)
No double taxation agreement (DTA) between Samoa and the PRC is currently in force; STEC preferential trade arrangements not applicable to shipyard goods

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (No.10 of 1987), as amended (including International Companies Amendment Acts 2016/2017 requiring confidential beneficial ownership registers); Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing Prevention Act 2018 (MLTFPA 2018); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2018; Samoa FIU AML/CFT Directives and Guidance Notes; International Companies (Fees) Regulations; Shipping Act 2012 (for maritime operating licenses); Hague Apostille Convention 1961 (Samoa acceded 9 May 2018; in force 9 September 2018).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (UBO register is confidential and maintained by the licensed registered agent; not publicly searchable; disclosable only to the Registrar of International Companies, Samoa FIU, and lawful enforcement authorities)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copy and identity certificate of each UBO and each director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence (PRC/HKSAR as applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs, effective 7 November 2023; HKSAR High Court for Hong Kong-issued documents). Consular Legalization via Embassy of Samoa in Beijing or MFAT Apia only if origin state is not an Apostille party.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille as above; Consular Legalization fallback as above

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of wealth declaration for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing clearing bank and notary public; signed by UBO before notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille as above; Consular Legalization fallback as above

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Register of Members/Directors of the ultimate holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or corporate registry of the parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille as above; Consular Legalization fallback as above

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the corporate shareholder or ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the parent entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille as above; Consular Legalization fallback as above

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/CFT compliance undertaking and beneficial ownership declaration executed by each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille as above; Consular Legalization fallback as above

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD/EDD under MLTFPA 2018 and FIU Directives: (i) PEP determination per statutory definition covering domestic/foreign PEPs, family members, and known close associates, with any PEP match requiring senior management approval and source-of-funds verification; (ii) continuous screening against OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT sanctions, and Samoa FIU national risk-based list; (iii) screening re-run at least every 30 days during pre-incorporation; (iv) UBO identification by ownership/control test at 25% plus control-in-fact; (v) mandatory enhanced due diligence (EDD) for the maritime/shipyard industry, maritime installment LCs, and escrow payment rails; (vi) all screening results documented in a file ready for FIU/Registrar inspection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: MCIL Samoa Companies Office - Samoa Companies Online Registry (Registrar of International Companies); all filings submitted through a licensed international company service provider via the MCIL Companies Office, Apia.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be entirely in Latin script (English or Samoan) and must end with the statutory suffix 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Societe Anonyme' or an accepted abbreviation such as 'Ltd.', 'Corp.', 'Inc.'. Chinese-character trading names may be used only as a secondary/trading name and must be filed with a certified Romanized transliteration and English translation; the Certificate of Incorporation is issued in English.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banking, Finance, Financial Services - prior license from Central Bank of Samoa under International Banking Act 2005 required
Trust, Trustee, Trust Company - prior trust license under International Trusts Act 1987 required
Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance, Underwriters - prior license under Insurance Act 2016 required
Government, Crown, State, Ministry, Cabinet - implies state patronage; prior MCIL/Cabinet consent required
Samoa or Samoan as a distinguishing element - requires consent to avoid misleading public register
Cooperative, Chamber of Commerce - prohibited absent separate statutory registration
Any token that is identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered company name in Samoa
Any token that is contrary to public policy, moral, or suggestive of unlawful activity, including terms implying weapons/trafficking operations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the licensed agent receives a written refusal notice stating statutory grounds. Procedure: (1) file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of refusal, supported by a statutory declaration and any corrective evidence; (2) for similarity-based refusals, submit a notarized letter of no objection/consent from the existing name holder; (3) for sensitive tokens, apply in writing to MCIL and, where applicable, to the Central Bank of Samoa or relevant licensing authority for prior ministerial approval; (4) if the Registrar affirms the refusal, apply for judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa within 21 days under the Judicature Act 1961; (5) a further 30-day name reservation extension may be requested through the licensed agent upon payment of the applicable MCIL renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially Permissible - the International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the licensed address of its international company service provider; a purely virtual or PO-Box address is not acceptable as the statutory registered office. The shipyard business may be conducted entirely extraterritorially (Samoa ICs are prohibited from carrying on business with Samoan residents without approval), so no physical industrial premises in Samoa is required for offshore contracting, LC, and escrow structures. If the IC elects to operate an actual physical shipyard within Samoa, a commercial premises license and local business registration are mandatory and a virtual office is not permissible for that licensed physical operation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Statutory registered office (agent address) audit probability is low (approximately 5-10% annually, triggered by FIU/Registrar AML file review). If a physical shipyard operation is established on-island, unannounced inspection likelihood is high (approximately 70%) under the Shipping Act 2012 and MCIL enforcement powers.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille fee of approximately USD 55

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese-to-English translation of corporate and UBO documents
Pre-incorporation legal due diligence and UBO-derived KYC opinion

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Maritime installment LC and escrow payment structure legal memorandum (pre-incorporation)
Conditional Samoa shipyard/maritime operating license fee (payable only if on-island operations commence)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), Sections 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 24 and 26; International Companies Regulations 1988; Business License Act 1998; Planning and Urban Management Act 2004; Occupational Safety and Health Act 2015
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Application for Incorporation of an International Company, together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association, culminating in the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a single subscriber share at nominal par value suffices. No escrow or capital deposit is mandated by the International Companies Act 1987; escrow and maritime installment letters of credit are adopted as target payment rails for shipyard construction contracts.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company be and is hereby ratified, and that the allotment of one ordinary share at par value to the initial subscriber be approved and recorded in the register of members; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office situated at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and the appointment of the registered agent, be confirmed and adopted; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Director Name] be appointed director, and [Secretary Name] be appointed secretary, each to hold office until replaced; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors be and are hereby authorized to open escrow accounts, negotiate maritime installment letters of credit, execute shipyard licensing applications, and any ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – Name Clearance Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request with the proposed corporate name (including 'Limited'), accompanied by two alternative names. SIFA screens the name against the register of existing international companies and prohibited terms. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form
Certificate of identity and due diligence questionnaire of the beneficial owner
Business profile describing the shipyard and vessel construction scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the Registrar issues written reasons; the applicant may request reconsideration in writing within 14 days or resubmit alternative names without additional state fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legal counsel drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English with a broad commercial shipbuilding objects clause. The initial subscriber executes the Memorandum and Articles before a notary public or licensed agent; the agent attests the signature and prepares the Declaration of Compliance.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (English, executed)
Notarized signature page of the subscriber
Declaration of Compliance signed by the registered agent
Consent to act of the first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the objects clause or draft wording, the agent amends and re-executes the charter documents and resubmits within the initial review window at no additional state fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed agent files Form 1 (Application for Incorporation) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, consent documents, and Declaration of Compliance, and pays the USD 100 official government filing fee through the SIFA registry window or online portal.
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Application for Incorporation
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association (two copies)
Declaration of Compliance
Consents of director and secretary
Registered agent consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA issues a requisition or query, the applicant must supply the requested supplementary information within 14 days; failure to cure may result in deemed withdrawal of the application, with the state fee refunded less any administrative charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registrar reviews the complete application, approves the company name, and issues a sealed Certificate of Incorporation. The International Company is constituted on the date of the Certificate; thereafter the registered agent obtains certified copies of the charter documents.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued by SIFA)
Certified copies of the Memorandum and Articles of Association (stamped)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a typographical or clerical error, the applicant may apply to the Registrar for correction and re-issuance upon payment of the prescribed nominal amendment fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Registered Office and Registered Agent in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the registered agent agreement and registered office consent at the agent's premises in Apia. The registered office address is filed with SIFA, and the statutory registers (members, directors, charges) are maintained at that office.
required_dossiers: Registered office consent form
Registered agent agreement
Register of members and register of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event the registered agent resigns or is removed, the company must appoint a successor licensed agent and file the notice of change with SIFA within 21 days to maintain statutory compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Banking Setup and Industrial License Kickoff
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; Licensed Commercial Bank; Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the statutory first board meeting to adopt the board resolutions ratifying incorporation, share allotment, registered office and officer appointments. Open a corporate bank account with escrow capability and maritime letter of credit facilities. Submit the Business License application and commercial shipyard operating license application to MCIL to commence the operational licensing phase.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution (minutes)
Certificate of Incorporation and charter documents
Passport copies and proof of address of directors and shareholder
Commercial bank account opening package and AML/KYC forms
Business License application and shipyard operating license application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank defers or declines the account on AML/KYC grounds, the applicant strengthens the due diligence package with a corporate structure chart, source of wealth evidence, and professional reference letters, and resubmits for the bank's compliance committee approval.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Business License Division, in conjunction with the Maritime Division of the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Shipyard Operating License and Business License (Business License Act 1998) for shipbuilding and vessel construction, repair, dry-docking and outfitting operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) – Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Report – Category A (Major Activity) under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004; Development Consent is required prior to shipyard construction and operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Treated industrial wastewater: pH 6.0-9.0, total suspended solids ≤ 50 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L; zero discharge of dry-dock, blasting or painting effluent to coastal and marine waters; VOC and particulate emissions from coating and abrasive blasting operations controlled via capture and filtration systems; hazardous wastes (solvents, paint residues, spent blasting media) managed under MNRE hazardous waste manifesting and disposed at licensed facilities; compliance with MARPOL 73/78 (Annexes I, V and VI) for vessel-related operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA); building and structural-load inspection and certification through PUMA Building Control; Occupational Safety and Health Clearance Certificate under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2015 issued by MCIL, including crane and lifting equipment certification, confined-space entry protocols, emergency response plans, and workplace registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa, which administers the Tax Administration Act 2012, Income Tax Act 2013, Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) Act 1993, Customs Duty Act 2014 and Excise Duty Act 2013. The MfR combines the former Inland Revenue Department and Customs Division, operates the official taxpayer portal at www.revenue.gov.ws, and uses UNCTAD ASYCUDA World as the electronic customs single window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An International Company (IC) must obtain a statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) from the Ministry for Revenue when it commences any taxable activity or importation in Samoa, or engages local staff; an otherwise pure offshore IC may be issued a TIN on application even without local nexus because a TIN is required before MfR will process VAGST refunds or zero-rating claims. The standard procedure is: (i) verify nexus or threshold, being commencement of taxable activity, WST 50,000 VAGST turnover, or any customs import; (ii) file the prescribed TIN application through the revenue portal with the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of International Companies within the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, evidence of the Samoan registered office and registered agent, a certified extract of directors and beneficial owners, and proof of non-resident ownership; (iii) MfR issues the TIN and annotates the taxpayer register to reflect the IC's non-resident or exempt status; and (iv) the IC also obtains a customs client or declarant code in ASYCUDA World for any import or export transactions. The IC must keep its annual international company registration and government fee current, as lapse can invalidate the exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: an IC validly incorporated and currently registered under Samoa's International Companies Act 1988 is statutorily exempt from Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, gift duty and estate duty on offshore activities and distributions to non-resident shareholders; it is not a pass-through entity and does not pay entity-level tax on qualifying offshore income. The exemption is territorial in effect: it does not apply to a Samoan-source taxable business, and the IC remains liable for VAGST at 15% on imports and local taxable supplies, customs duty on shipyard machinery and materials, and wage withholding if local staff are engaged. The classification is automatic for a compliant IC and is not an elective status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) acting in its capacity as the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Exchange Control Regulations made pursuant to the Foreign Exchange Act 1978, as amended and supplemented by CBS prudential and AML/CFT directives.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tala (WST) is not a fully freely convertible currency under a liberalised capital account. Current account transactions are generally permitted through authorised dealers (licensed commercial banks) without individual CBS approval, subject to documentary verification and post-transaction reporting. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity injections for an International Company shipyard, loan advances, issuance of guarantees covering maritime instalments, and offshore hedging with derivatives, require either prior written CBS exchange control approval or an express exemption certificate obtained under the International Companies regime. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is structurally permitted and free of withholding tax for International Companies, but CBS and the clearing bank will apply practical hurdles: proof that the distributed profits originated from verified export proceeds or trade receivables, board resolution and distribution ledger, audited financial statements, and the absence of overdue domestic obligations. In practice, approvals are granted on a case-by-case basis and can take 5–15 business days; there is no blanket current-account convertibility guarantee for non-resident owned entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBS Exchange Control Regulations, resident exporters and, by extension, Samoa-registered International Companies maintaining Samoan-authorised-dealer accounts are required to repatriate export proceeds relating to Samoan-sourced trade to an authorised dealer in Samoa within 180 days from the bill of lading or invoice date. The mandatory conversion ratio is 100% of the foreign currency invoice value into WST for export contracts executed wholly or partly within Samoa, unless a CBS exemption certificate is issued. For an International Company engaged in ocean-container-vessel construction where the vessel is fabricated in a foreign subcontracted shipyard, the export proceeds are classified as offshore trade receipts, and the surrender rule may be suspended or reduced to zero if the entity provides the underlying construction agreement, overseas cost breakdown, bill of lading, carrier contract, and a CBS exemption confirmation evidencing that the transaction does not create a net domestic WST cash flow requirement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Samoa does not maintain a standalone electronic money institution (EMI) licensing regime, and no offshore digital EMI is permitted to provide payment or clearing services in Samoa without a CBS banking or financial services license. An International Company may connect a foreign-licensed EMI only as a non-regulated front-end payment gateway, but the actual clearing and custody must be held through a CBS-licensed authorised dealer. In practical terms, the execution of maritime instalment LC and escrow arrangements requires a full commercial bank relationship in Samoa, and reliance on an unlicensed EMI would trigger adverse AML and correspondent de-risking outcomes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident owned International Company, CBS AML rules and the internal KYC policies of tier-1 banks generally require at least one natural-person director and the ultimate beneficial owner to undergo a physical in-person KYC interview at a Samoan branch. Fully remote account opening is not available for new corporate relationships. However, if the company has a locally resident director or a Samoan licensed attorney-in-fact who is an authorised signatory under an executed power of attorney, banks may permit the remaining non-resident directors and beneficial owners to be interviewed via videoconference, subject to notarised and apostilled identity documents, independent verification of the corporate registry records, and certified true copies of board resolutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company domiciled in Samoa with tax-exempt designation and no substantial local operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full constitutional documents and corporate registry extract from the Registrar of International Companies; board resolution approving physical bank presence; notarised and apostilled passports of directors and beneficial owners; certified organisational chart and source of wealth declaration; audited financial statements for the preceding two years; and a comprehensive business plan evidencing the shipyard contract pipeline, counterparty due diligence and the commercial purpose of the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shipbuilding transaction complexity, modest initial capital and high-value maritime instalment collections routed from non-resident buyers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed container-vessel construction contract and vessel specification annex; payment schedule reconciling each instalment with the stage of construction; letters of intent from third-party subcontractors; classification society documents covering the vessel design; risk-rated customer analysis; in-house AML risk assessment of each buyer; and a cash-flow projection showing that each inbound payment is matched against verifiable progress milestones.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or nominee shareholder arrangement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Form B083 beneficial ownership register, nominee declaration and the underlying trust or foundation deed (redacted where necessary); KYC forms for all ultimate natural persons owning or controlling in excess of 10%; sworn statutory declarations from the directors; consent letters from the nominee confirming legal and beneficial ownership separation; and a clear written explanation of the ownership structure signed by the legal counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually large initial capital injection or rapid expected turnover inconsistent with the global manufacturing profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital verification report issued by a Samoan registered auditor; source-of-funds confirmation from the sending bank referencing the exact purpose code; equity subscription agreement and bank statement evidencing the transfer; board-approved treasury policy; sub-contractual work orders and pro-forma invoices for the first construction phases; and documentary evidence that the projected turnover reflects a defined vessel order book rather than a high-velocity unaudited cash flow.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from a parent company or strategic investor must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 into a designated WST or USD account maintained with an authorised dealer in Samoa. The remitting bank must use an accurate purpose code — where available, 701110 for cash capital contributions or 702112 for equity capital in a finance/industry holding; for maritime instalments, the underlying invoice should be referenced under a transport equipment purpose such as 102101 (seagoing vessels). Prior to execution, the International Company must submit to the receiving bank a CBS exchange control approval or exemption certificate, a board resolution authorising the account and the remittance, a notarised copy of the investor's identity and constitutional documents, and the vessel construction contract or investment agreement evidencing the commercial transaction. The receiving bank will perform a funds-arrival verification, record the capital against CBS reporting thresholds, and issue a certificate of receipt for local corporate registry and audit purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements to overseas shipbuilders, dry-dock subcontractors, engine suppliers, steel fabricators and classification surveyors should be settled under SWIFT MT103 for non-documentary operational payments, MT100/MT202 for interbank transfers covering letter-of-credit reimbursements, and a Samoa-law-governed irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (CL C) for staged vessel financing. The LC must be issued in favour of the subcontractor or equipment seller and advised through a UCP600-compliant channel (MT700/MT720). Where the LC maturity exceeds 180 days, CBS pre-approval of the deferred payment term is required. All outbound payments must be supported by the underlying construction invoice, signed schedule of work acceptance, shipping or delivery documents, and a negative media/sanctions screening result for the beneficiary. Payments directed to restricted shipyards or individuals are automatically blocked under CBS-approved sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla forward contracts in USD/WST booked with a CBS-licensed authorised dealer, covering actual and committed trade receivables and payables for vessel construction and shipyard consumables.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed in USD/WST through an offshore hedge counterparty, provided the underlying is an approved CBS-hedgeable exposure and settlement is made net in a permitted offshore clearing currency.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/WST) whereby the International Company exchanges fixed or floating payments with an authorised dealer, subject to CBS prior approval, supporting matched debt-service and vessel-instalment cashflow conversion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Samoa International Companies Act 1987, s.190) together with Annual Government Renewal Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: due on each anniversary of incorporation, with a 90-day grace period before the Registrar classifies the company as delinquent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of 10% of the annual fee per month of delay (minimum WST 300, approx. USD 115); non-payment for 6 consecutive months empowers the Registrar to strike off the company administratively; reinstatement requires payment of arrears plus a reinstatement fee of approx. annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation filed with the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent (maintainer of the UBO Register) and Registrar of International Companies, MCIL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the Annual Return; updates to shareholdings must be lodged within 14 business days of any transfer during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to WST 3,000 (approx. USD 1,150) and/or 12 months imprisonment for directors/officers; continued non-compliance constitutes a ground for administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Notification / Substance Return (shipping and shipbuilding treated as relevant activity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Ministry for Revenue, jointly with the Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after the end of the financial year, as prescribed by the Ministry for Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of WST 10,000 (approx. USD 3,850) for late or non-filing; persistent default is reported to the Registrar and may trigger de-registration under the International Companies Act 1987

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies unless the International Company qualifies as a small company under ss.76-77 of the International Companies Act 1987: not more than 20 registered members, gross annual income not exceeding WST 1,000,000 (approx. USD 380,000), and total assets not exceeding WST 1,000,000 (approx. USD 380,000). A commercial shipyard vehicle of this scale will exceed the income/asset thresholds and must appoint an IPSA-qualified auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Samoa (true and fair view requirement); the Act also permits US GAAP for international companies provided the accounts disclose the basis of preparation and give a true and fair view. Accounts must be maintained in English with amounts in Tala or US Dollars.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2019 and the International Companies Act 1987, the registered agent must obtain each year a written confirmation of the ultimate beneficial owner, verify all share transfers executed during the year, and attach the confirmation to the Annual Return filed with the Registrar. Failure to keep the beneficial ownership register current invalidates any transfer notice and exposes the company to sanctions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (maintained at the registered office in Samoa)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 per annum (consolidated shipyard holding vehicle)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for International Company (full statutory exemption); standard resident corporate income tax headline rate: 27%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies Act 1987, s.224: total exemption from corporate income tax, capital gains tax, dividend/interest/royalty withholding taxes, stamp duty and estate duty on all IC income, profits, gains and distributions; annual government registration fee is the sole fiscal charge

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IC-AR/ESD (International Company Annual Return and Economic Substance Declaration) filed with the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa; lodging through a licensed registered agent or directly at the MCIL Companies Registry; no separate corporate income tax return is required of a tax-exempt IC
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before each anniversary of the date of incorporation; the annual government fee must be paid simultaneously and no extension of the filing window is granted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International Company registration number and exact corporate name, including former names or transliterations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the IC number as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation; no Samoan tax file number or foreign tax identification number is required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in Samoa and particulars of the licensed registered agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered office must be located in Samoa; a non-resident IC may state only the registered agent's address and must ensure the agent holds a valid power of attorney

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential addresses, nationality and passport details of all directors and the secretary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident natural-person directors are permitted; provide complete foreign residential addresses and passport numbers for anti-money laundering verification

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized share capital, paid-up capital and the currency in which the share capital is expressed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum capital is required; declare the capital in US dollars or Samoan Tala; the authorized capital amount determines the annual government fee class

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code and a factual description of the commercial operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the shipbuilding scope, insert: 'construction, repair and sale of deep-sea dry cargo and container vessels (ISIC 3011)' and confirm no shipping or chartering revenue is derived

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Economic substance declaration: confirmation of whether the IC carries on a relevant activity under the Economic Substance Regulations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pure shipbuilding is not an ESR-listed relevant activity; if the IC also operates vessels engaged in maritime transport or earns shipping income, the 'shipping' category must be declared and evidenced

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: If a relevant activity is declared: gross income from the activity, Samoan employee headcount and qualifications, registered premises details and annual operating expenditure in Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Submit Samoan payroll records, lease agreements and audited or management accounts; personnel located wholly outside Samoa will not count toward substance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compliance declaration covering the International Companies Act, anti-money laundering obligations and accuracy of the beneficial ownership register
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To be signed by a director or by the registered agent under power of attorney; any false or misleading statement is a criminal offence

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Immediate 10% surcharge on the unpaid annual fee plus a WST 500 late-filing penalty; continued default attracts compounded default penalties, administrative strike-off from the International Companies Register, disqualification of defaulting directors and a prohibition on maintaining bank accounts in Samoa

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an exempt International Company to non-resident shareholders (International Companies Act 1987, s.224); standard domestic dividend withholding tax rate for taxable resident Samoan companies: 15%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No treaty relief application is required for dividends paid by an International Company because the statutory IC exemption eliminates withholding tax at source. Where a dividend is paid by a taxable Samoan resident payer, the non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain a certificate of tax residence (TRC) from the treaty partner tax authority; (2) file a Form WHT-DTA relief application with the Samoan Inland Revenue Division prior to payment; (3) deliver a beneficial ownership declaration to the Samoan payer; and (4) preserve the TRC for five years. Samoa's DTAs with Australia, New Zealand and Norway, and the China-Samoa DTA where in force, generally reduce portfolio dividends to 15% and direct-investment dividends (shareholding of 10% or more) to 5%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates under the Income Tax Act 2012: interest 15%, royalties 15%. Treaty rates: Australia, New Zealand and Norway - interest 10%, royalties 10%; China - interest 10%, royalties 10% subject to the treaty's entry into force. Payments made by an exempt International Company are wholly outside the withholding net, and therefore no WHT is levied on outbound royalties or interest paid by the IC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable to a tax-exempt International Company; for any taxable Samoan affiliate, transfer pricing documentation (Local File) is mandatory where annual connected-party turnover exceeds WST 5,000,000, and a Master File is advisable where worldwide group turnover exceeds WST 100,000,000; failure to produce documentation attracts a penalty of WST 100,000 plus a 20% uplift on any assessed adjustment
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) 2019-2021 apply to International Companies carrying on relevant activities, which include shipping and maritime transport. A shipyard engaged purely in shipbuilding (ISIC 3011) is not itself a relevant activity, but the doctrine is triggered if the IC derives shipping income from vessel ownership, chartering, crew management or haulage. If triggered, the IC must demonstrate in Samoa: (1) board meetings with a quorum held in Samoa and strategic decisions recorded in Samoan minutes; (2) core income-generating activities performed in Samoa; (3) adequate employees, physical premises and operating expenditure in Samoa. Compliance is certified annually via Form IC-AR/ESD; no corporate income tax or payroll tax is imposed on the substantive operations of the exempt IC.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Fraud and False Economic Substance Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a materially false economic substance declaration, falsely claiming Samoan management, personnel or expenditure for ship operations; concealing ultimate beneficial ownership in order to preserve the tax-exempt International Company status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to WST 1,000,000 against the company and WST 100,000 against responsible officers, imprisonment up to 7 years, compulsory deregistration, and automatic recovery of tax at the 27% CIT rate on worldwide income for the non-compliant years; referral to foreign tax authorities under the multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for restitution of avoided tax and penalties; travel restriction orders under the Tax Administration Act; director disqualification for up to 10 years; foreign directors placed on immigration blacklists and exposed to extradition in aggravated fraud cases

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An International Company carrying on shipping-related activities without any employees, office premises or Samoan management; use of the exempt IC as a pure paper vehicle to channel non-resident shipping profits without substance, triggering OECD/EU harmful tax practice review
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic substance non-compliance penalty of WST 10,000 up to WST 75,000, or WST 250,000 for a repeat offence; automatic exchange of information with the shareholder's tax jurisdiction under CRS; strike-off from the International Companies Register within 90 days of default; loss of limited liability for obligations incurred after the default date
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for all company debts incurred following the default; civil recovery proceedings by the Registrar for unpaid penalties; personal travel bans while penalties remain outstanding; custodial sentence up to 5 years for continuing refusal to remedy the substance failure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Fraudulent Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using shipyard installment letters of credit or escrow accounts to launder proceeds of crime, inflating or deflating hull construction invoices, executing fake related-party vessel sales with artificial transfer pricing, or failing to maintain an accurate beneficial ownership register
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the AML/CFT Act 2018 (as amended): fines up to WST 2,000,000, imprisonment up to 14 years, or both; revocation of any International Service Provider licence; freezing and forfeiture of vessel assets, letter of credit proceeds and escrow balances; confiscation under the Proceeds of Crime Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners prosecuted personally for money laundering; civil and criminal liability for arranging false letter of credit documentation; personal bankruptcy orders; prohibition from managing any Samoan International Company for up to 15 years; extradition exposure for non-resident directors acting with fraudulent intent

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Annual Return / Non-Payment of Annual Fee
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-payment of the prescribed annual government fee or failure to lodge Form IC-AR/ESD within the anniversary filing window; continuing to trade after administrative strike-off
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic 10% late-payment surcharge; mandatory termination of services by the registered agent; administrative dissolution after 6 months in default; penalty up to WST 5,000 plus a WST 1,000 restoration fee; unauthorized trading after deregistration constitutes an offence attracting a daily fine of WST 500
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for unpaid annual fees, penalties and all contracts entered into in the company's name after deregistration; Samoan courts may enforce judgments against personal assets and issue departure prohibition orders against non-resident directors
